newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-RESCUE PLAN PROPOSED FOR ENGLAND'S MILLWALL.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-RESCUE PLAN PROPOSED FOR ENGLAND'S MILLWALL.

text.p: English second division club Millwall's future may be guaranteed under a 10 million pound ($16.2 million) rescue bid unveiled on Friday.

Greek-Cypriot businessman Theo Paphitis, head of a high street stationery chain, will become chairman of the London club if the plan is approved by shareholders. Paphitis is currently chairman of minor league club Walton & Hersham.
Millwall are aiming to raise the funds through the issue of new shares, earmarking 7.25 million pounds to pay off debts and leaving the rest as working capital.

Millwall joined the stock market in 1989, helping to set a trend which many other clubs have since followed. But the move to an expensive new stadium was accompanied by a slump on the pitch, resulting in relegation last season.
Trading in the club's shares was suspended in January when it was forced to call in an administrator to run its business as its financial crisis worsened.

The club has since sacked manager Jimmy Nicholl and chief executive Graham Hortop and transfer listed 11 players in a bid to stem its losses. It is resigned to spending another season in the second division after its promotion challenge faded away in recent weeks. ($ = 0.616 British Pounds)
